task: Harden bootstrap CSI NFS sidecars and CPU limits; retain only exact measured CIS exceptions.

events.summary: Scope is the bootstrap-only csi-driver-nfs 4.13.2 release, exact portal Config Audit rules/reasons, R417, and corresponding documentation. No GitOps Application is involved.

provenance: Owner supplied live single-node measurements from 2026-11-26: root NFS plugin created a root:root 0755 CSI socket in the shared socket-dir; controller non-root sidecars cannot connect; NFS mount plugin is privileged with SYS_ADMIN; controller workingMountDir is /tmp.
Owner supplied actionable KSV findings and existing exact accepted checks for csi-nfs-node and csi-nfs-controller.
Inspected offline chart copy .review/charts/csi-driver-nfs, including 4.13.2 values and hardcoded template security contexts.
events.summary: Measured socket ownership/mode and privileged mount requirement justify only the retained UID/connectivity and privileged mount exceptions. KSV125 remains actionable because registry trust is a separate decision.

Initial R417 only invoked the renderer script directly, so it did not exercise Helm plugin resolution. Owner reproduced the fresh-install failure on Helm v4.2.1: `helm upgrade --post-renderer /tmp/csi-nfs-postrender.sh` failed with `plugin: {Name:/tmp/csi-nfs-postrender.sh Type:postrenderer/v1} not found`. Owner verified the v4 plugin.yaml format and named-plugin render on v4.3.2; the test environment uses HELM_DATA_HOME and HELM_PLUGINS under one temporary root.

Bootstrap now installs/reconciles the `csi-nfs-postrender` postrenderer/v1 plugin from the scripts tree before upgrade and passes its plugin name to Helm 4. Plugin metadata and script live in scripts/cluster/lib/helm-plugins/csi-nfs-postrender. The original sidecar and 100m CPU hardening is retained.
